approach: Resolve the initial velocity and gravity along and perpendicular to the incline, then use the perpendicular equation for the time and the along-incline equation for the range.

steps.text: Take axes along the incline, up the slope, and perpendicular to it. Resolve the initial velocity using the 30° angle between the velocity and the incline surface.
steps.equation: along the incline: 20√2 cos30°; perpendicular to it: 20√2 sin30°

steps.text: Resolve the acceleration due to gravity along the same two axes, using the 45° incline angle.
steps.equation: along the incline: −g sin45°; perpendicular to it: −g cos45°

steps.text: The particle returns to the incline when the perpendicular displacement is zero again; solve for the time of flight.
Find the along-incline displacement at this time, which is the range measured along the incline.
State the results; this is the final answer.

final_answer.value: time of flight = 4 s, range along the incline ≈ 41.41 m

common_mistakes.text: Using the 30° angle as if it were measured from the horizontal, without adding the 45° incline angle, gives a wrong time of about 2.83 s.
